Title: Traffic crawls along 20km stretch entering Kelantan as school break and National Day surge builds
Article:
GUA MUSANG, Aug 29 — Traffic entering Kelantan has been reported to be moving slowly along a stretch of about 20 kilometres at the border entry point between Merapoh, Pahang, and Kampung Mentara, Gua Musang, due to an increase in vehicles in conjunction with the school holidays and National Day celebration this Monday.
Gua Musang district police chief Supt Sik Choon Foo said traffic police personnel and the Mobile Patrol Vehicle (MPV) unit have been deployed to the location to conduct regular patrols.
“Police are closely monitoring traffic flow along all major routes to ensure the safety and smooth movement of road users.
“Congestion was detected at the diversion area of the Central Spine Road construction project, causing traffic to slow down from Merapoh to the end of the highway at Kampung Mentara,” he told Bernama today.
However, he said traffic flow returned to normal after passing the diversion area.
“So far, the number of vehicles on the road is indeed high, but traffic in Gua Musang town remains smooth without any unusual congestion,” he said.
Meanwhile, a Bernama check around 5pm today in Gua Musang town heading towards Kuala Krai found traffic to be smooth despite an increase in the number of vehicles since this morning.
In an earlier statement, PLUS Malaysia Berhad (PLUS) said traffic on its highways is expected to reach 2.2 million vehicles on peak days between Aug 28 and 31 and Sept 4 and 7 in conjunction with the National Day celebration and school holidays.
PLUS also advised road users to plan their journeys by referring to the MyPLUS-TTA digital travel schedule via the PLUS App to help distribute traffic flow and reduce vehicle concentration during peak periods. — Bernama

Title: ‘We can only pray’: Family of missing Malaysian in Nepal tragedy anxiously awaits news
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 29 — “Only prayer and patience can strengthen our spirits,” lamented Mures, the eldest son of senior citizen K. Balasingam, 71, who has yet to be contacted following the flash flood disaster on the Nepal-Tibet border on Wednesday.
Mures, 40, said his father’s journey to perform a religious ceremony on Mount Kailash, Tibet turned into a terrifying nightmare for the family after he was last seen active on the WhatsApp application on the morning of the incident.
“My father alone joined a group with 16 other Malaysians to Mount Kailash in Tibet, China to perform a religious ceremony.
“He arrived there on August 23 and was supposed to return to Malaysia on September 6 but until now our family has not received any information about him after the incident,” he said when contacted by Bernama today.
Describing his father’s personality, Mures described the former businessman in the transport sector who hails from Negeri Sembilan as someone who is very active in leisure and religious activities despite his age.
He said the family had contacted various parties to obtain the latest information including the Malaysian Embassy in Kathmandu and the police.
“So far we are still patient and do not know how long we will have to wait for developments regarding my father.
“We also received information from a member of the group who is in Nepal but until now there is no latest news. We continue to pray that my father is safe,” he said.
Balasingam was among 17 Malaysians in a group managed by Nepal-based travel agency Fishtail Tours & Travels.
The Foreign Ministry today said 55 Malaysians were still unreachable following the devastating flash floods and landslides in Rasuwa District, Nepal, on Wednesday. — Bernama

Title: Air quality worsens, two Sarawak stations breach very unhealthy levels, 29 areas nationwide unhealthy
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 29 — Two monitoring stations in Sarawak recorded very unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 4pm today, while 29 other areas nationwide registered unhealthy air quality.
According to data from the Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, the API readings at Sri Aman and the Serian district police headquarters (IPD) monitoring station reached 229 and 228, respectively.
Areas recording unhealthy API levels included Sarikei in Sarawak (194), Sungai Petani in Kedah (161), Cheras in Kuala Lumpur (160), Minden in Penang (158), Taiping in Perak (158), Shah Alam in Selangor (157), Putrajaya (155), Seremban in Negeri Sembilan (151), and Segamat in Johor (132).
Meanwhile, 36 areas recorded moderate air quality, including Pegoh Ipoh in Perak (99), Banting in Selangor (95), Bukit Rambai in Melaka (92), Tangkak in Johor (90), Besut in Terengganu (88), Kota Bharu in Kelantan (87), and Kota Kinabalu in Sabah (86).
An API reading of zero to 50 indicates good air quality, 51 to 100 (moderate), 101 to 200 (unhealthy), 201 to 300 (very unhealthy), and above 300 (hazardous).
API figures are updated hourly based on readings from 68 monitoring stations nationwide. — Bernama

Title: MetMalaysia warns of thunderstorms and heavy rain in six states and KL until 7pm
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 29 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has warned of thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds in seven states and Kuala Lumpur until 7pm today.
MetMalaysia said the warning was issued for the entire state of Kelantan and 11 districts in Perak: Batang Padang, Muallim, Hulu Perak, Kuala Kangsar, Kinta, Kampar, Perak Tengah, Larut Matang, Selama, Hilir Perak and Bagan Datuk.
The warning also covers Hulu Terengganu, Dungun, Besut, Setiu, Kuala Nerus, Kuala Terengganu and Marang in Terengganu, and Lipis, Cameron Highlands, Rompin, Raub, Bentong, Jerantut and Temerloh in Pahang.
The two other states affected are Selangor, covering Sabak Bernam, Kuala Selangor, Hulu Selangor, Gombak and Petaling, and Johor, covering Kluang, Mersing, Kota Tinggi and Segamat. — Bernama

Title: Anwar says Malaysia’s success must be anchored by a knowledgeable, disciplined generation
Article:
BATU KAWAN, Aug 29 — A country’s success should not be measured solely by economic and technological progress, but must also be supported by the development of a knowledgeable and disciplined younger generation, said Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
The Prime Minister said young people should be provided with an education that also instils values, a spirit of service and a sense of responsibility towards their families, society and country.
“What is the meaning of development, what is the meaning of a country’s success if our children are not instilled with spirit, education, discipline and love? That is why our children must have such a spirit.
“Why do we acquire knowledge at schools, institutions of higher learning and universities? It is to become knowledgeable and morally upright individuals who are able to serve society, their parents and also the country. This is a culture that must be nurtured,” he said.
Anwar said this when officiating the 15th Malaysian Scouts Jamboree (MYJAM15) at the Penang State Stadium here today. Also present were Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow and Chief Scout Datuk Prof Dr Mohd Zin Bidin.
Commenting on current challenges, Anwar said that in navigating the rapid advancement of information technology and artificial intelligence (AI), the younger generation must not neglect their cultural roots and values, which form the foundation of society.
He said technological changes must be accompanied by the ability of the younger generation to adapt to new challenges without sacrificing the values and heritage that shape their identity.
The Prime Minister also stressed the importance of fostering unity in diversity, given that the younger generation would be the country’s future leaders.
Ahead of the 2026 National Day celebrations, he also urged the younger generation to continue nurturing their spirit of patriotism and be prepared to face future tests and challenges.
MYJAM15, which runs from today until Sept 4, brings together more than 5,450 local and international scouts from 11 countries, including South Korea, Indonesia, Singapore and Sri Lanka.
This year’s jamboree also marks a milestone as the national event returns to Penang after 60 years, since the state first hosted the event in Teluk Bahang in 1966. — Bernama

Title: Desa ParkCity family tragedy takes new turn as police reveal illegal investment issue alongside alleged love scam
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 29 — Police investigating the deaths of a family of four at a Desa ParkCity condominium in Kepong have revealed that the couple had also become entangled in an illegal investment scheme, adding a new dimension to a case already linked to an alleged love scam and RM260,000 in losses and debt.
Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said relatives of the couple were aware of both issues.
“The family knew about the love scam problem and that they had become trapped in an illegal investment scheme.
“The allegations involving the love scam, the existence of a scammer, as well as the RM260,000 in losses and debts, are still under investigation,” he said in a statement today.
The latest disclosure broadens the financial circumstances police are examining following the deaths at the condominium in Desa ParkCity on Wednesday.
Yesterday, investigators said they were looking into whether pressure over the RM260,000 debt, after his wife allegedly fell victim to a love scam, could have driven the 48-year-old man to kill his wife, 47, and their two children, aged nine and seven, before taking his own life.
The speculation followed the discovery of a note believed to have been left by the father on the dining table of the family’s Desa ParkCity home.

Title: Wisma Putra: 55 Malaysians still uncontactable as checks expand to Nepal–China border areas
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 29 — Fifty-five Malaysians remain uncontactable following the floods and landslides that struck Rasuwa District, Nepal on August 26, according to Malaysia’s Foreign Ministry.
“Two Malaysians previously reported as uncontactable have since been contacted, and verification of the remaining cases is ongoing,” the ministry, widely known as Wisma Putra, said in its latest statement updating the situation in Nepal and surrounding areas.
The Embassy of Malaysia in Kathmandu continues to work with the Emergency Response Team of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Nepal, the Nepal Tourism Board, travel agencies and relevant local authorities.
“Search and rescue operations in Nepal remain ongoing, while authorities are also monitoring the risk of further water surges from the Tibet Autonomous Region, China,” it said.
As at 5.00 pm Nepal time (7.15 pm Malaysia time) August 28, 2026, the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority of Nepal reported that 771 people had been rescued, including 116 foreign nationals.
“Based on the official list available at this stage, no Malaysian has been identified among the foreign nationals rescued to date,” said Wisma Putra.
Wisma Putra said it has expanded its consular response to include Malaysians stranded in China due to travel disruptions arising from the floods and landslides in Nepal.
“A group of 72 Malaysians in Darchen, China, has been confirmed safe and in good health,” it said.
Wisma Putra said the Embassy of Malaysia in Beijing is in contact with the group, and their families are aware of their status.
“The Embassy is providing consular assistance, including support for their travel arrangements to leave the Tibet Autonomous Region, China,” it said.
Separately, the ministry said it had received information from the Chinese authorities and family members regarding 36 Malaysians who are currently reported as uncontactable in areas affected by telecommunications disruptions.
“The ministry is working closely with the Chinese authorities and family members to establish contact with the individuals concerned.
“The information is also being cross-checked against reports involving Malaysians in Nepal to identify any duplication as verification continues,” it said.
The Ministry’s Operations Room in Putrajaya has been operating around the clock since August 27, 2026, to coordinate information and assist Malaysians in the affected areas and their families.
Malaysians in the affected areas, as well as family members with relevant information, may contact the ministry through the following channels:
Ministry Of Foreign Affairs Operations Room
Phone number: +603 8887 4570
E-mail:
dutyofficer@kln.gov.my
The ministry urged the public not to speculate or share unverified information while efforts to establish the safety and whereabouts of the Malaysians concerned remain ongoing.
“Further updates will be provided based on verified information received through official channels,” said the ministry, noting that it continues to monitor developments closely. — Bernama

Title: Nearly RM250,000 payout after Segambut jogger fractures spine while fending off neighbour’s German Shepherds
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 29 — The owner of two German Shepherds has been ordered to pay nearly RM250,000 in damages after his neighbour fractured his spine while trying to protect himself from the dogs during a jogging incident five years ago.
Sinar Harian
reported that KL Sessions Court judge Zawiyah Saad found Datuk Seri Ong Thiam Boon liable for the February 10, 2021 incident involving his neighbour, Datuk Mohd Kamal Abdullah.
The court awarded Mohd Kamal RM178,457.60 in special damages and RM70,000 in general damages after a full trial.
Zawiyah reached the decision after considering witness testimony, documentary evidence and written submissions from both sides.
Ong was also ordered to pay interest of 5 per cent a year on the damages from the date of judgment until full settlement.
The court dismissed his counterclaim with costs and ordered him to pay a further RM15,000 in costs to Mohd Kamal.
In his lawsuit, Mohd Kamal alleged that two German Shepherds belonging to Ong attacked him while he was jogging at Taman Anjung Tiara in Segambut.
He said he fell while trying to protect himself from the dogs, fracturing his spine and later requiring surgery and follow-up treatment.
Mohd Kamal alleged that the incident was caused by Ong’s failure to properly control the animals and to ensure that the gate to his home remained closed.
Ong, however, denied that the dogs had attacked or even come into contact with Mohd Kamal.
According to his defence, Mohd Kamal lost his balance and fell while moving backwards on a steep and uneven road after swinging a walking stick at the two dogs.
Ong also argued that Mohd Kamal’s injuries were caused or contributed to by his own negligence.
In a counterclaim, Ong alleged that Mohd Kamal had threatened him, causing fear, humiliation and mental distress.
Mohd Kamal was represented by lawyer Shahril Madisa of Messrs Shahrul Hamidi & Haziq, while Ong was represented by Tan Shao Jia and Wong Win Xien of Messrs Manjit Singh Sachdev, Mohammad Radzi & Partners.

Title: Pakatan open to Bersatu tie-up for Melaka state election as Amirudin says ‘that is politics’
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 29 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) is open to working with Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia in the coming Melaka state election, Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said, signalling that even former political adversaries could become potential partners as parties manoeuvre ahead of the polls.
The
New Straits Times
reported that the PH election director said the coalition had no objection to considering cooperation with Bersatu or other parties if circumstances required it and if such an arrangement could help ensure political stability.
“Bersatu? If we can accept working with Umno, surely, we can accept Bersatu.
“For example, we previously worked with Umno, and before that, we worked with Bersatu.
“Then there was the Sheraton Move. PAS has also worked with Bersatu, PAS has separated from Bersatu, PAS has separated from Umno, and PAS has wanted to work with Umno. That is politics,” Amirudin told reporters after officiating the Madani Kita programme with the Ampang Jaya community today.
His remarks come amid increasingly fluid negotiations over the Melaka election, with PH and Barisan Nasional (BN) expected to discuss electoral cooperation while PAS has also reportedly held preliminary talks with Umno.
Bersatu, however, was reportedly excluded from those PAS-Umno discussions.
Amirudin, who is also Selangor menteri besar, suggested the shifting alliances need not necessarily be seen as a sign of political instability.
“If people see this as political uncertainty, then it is political uncertainty.
“But if people see it as a new form of political maturity, it could change Malaysia’s political landscape,” he said.
He said PH remained united and had previously shown that it was prepared to make compromises with other parties, including allowing BN to contest seats in Selangor that had previously been won by PH.
Amirudin said PH would prepare for various possibilities in Melaka while ensuring that cooperation within the coalition remained intact.
Any prospective alliance, he said, would have to be based on sincerity and a clear commitment to preserving the stability and prosperity achieved under the unity government.
He also invoked the political turmoil that followed the Sheraton Move in 2020, which led to the collapse of the then PH federal government.
“We do not want to repeat that, and we need to establish a stable government,” he said.
Amirudin has been tasked with handling possible electoral cooperation between PH and BN in Melaka.
The current Melaka state assembly’s term expires at the end of December, with an election required within 60 days of its dissolution.
BN chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has previously said the coalition intends to defend all 21 seats it won in the 2021 Melaka election, while remaining open to electoral cooperation.
BN won 21 of the state assembly’s 28 seats in that election, while PH secured five and Perikatan Nasional (PN) two.
PAS president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang has meanwhile said PN would drop cooperation with BN if BN chose to contest alongside PH.

Title: BNM warns of scammers using phone numbers similar to STR, Sara hotlines and impersonating MoF officials
Article:
KUCHING, Aug 29 — Members of the public have been advised to remain vigilant against individuals impersonating officials from the Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) and Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (Sara) programmes.
Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM), in issuing the warning, said some criminal groups had resorted to using telephone numbers similar to official hotlines to contact members of the public and gain their trust before obtaining their personal and banking information.
“Some individuals are impersonating officials from the Ministry of Finance (MoF), claiming to represent the STR and Sara programmes, and contacting people using numbers similar to official phone numbers in an attempt to trick victims into providing personal information,” said BNM in a Facebook post.
BNM reminded all that the MoF has not authorised any third party to use its official contact numbers to handle STR or Sara matters, and that MoF officials would never ask the public to make any payments on their behalf.
The central bank appealed to the public not to disclose any personal or banking information to unidentified callers, including their MyKad number, bank account number, One-Time Password (OTP) or Transaction Authorisation Code (TAC), online banking password or Personal Identification Number (PIN), and other personal and financial information.
It also urged the public to adhere to the ‘3S’ anti-fraud principle: Soal (inquire), Sekat (block) and Sebar (share).
The public must first inquire about and verify the information and identity provided by the caller; subsequently, they must never provide personal or banking information to strangers; and lastly, they should inform friends and family about the scam and report it to the enforcement authorities to help prevent more people from falling prey to scammers.
“If a person unfortunately falls victim to fraud, he/she should immediately contact his/her bank’s hotline to request assistance in blocking suspicious transactions.
“The victim should also call the National Scam Response Centre (NSRC) at 997 for assistance and report the incident to the police for further investigation,” pointed out BNM.
The central bank also advised the public to immediately end any suspicious call claiming to be from officials of the STR or SARA programmes.
They should then contact the relevant authorities through official channels to verify the caller’s identity and the information provided.

Title: Printer apologises, says last-minute order led to incorrect Jalur Gemilang star worn by Kedah MB
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 29 — A printing company has blamed a rushed last-minute order and less thorough quality checks for an incorrect Jalur Gemilang star appearing on attire worn by Kedah Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor and several dignitaries at a Merdeka event.
Berita Harian
reported that NE Creative Ventures has apologised publicly to the Kedah Menteri Besar’s Office and accepted full responsibility for the mistake, after photographs of the attire went viral on social media.
The Ayer Keroh, Melaka-based company said an error during production resulted in the star on the printed Malaysian flag having fewer than the official 14 points.
“The design of the attire was printed based on the reference artwork file received before undergoing a technical tracing process during the production stage.
“We acknowledge that an oversight occurred after receiving an additional last-minute order to meet a tight deadline, resulting in the detailed checking process, or quality control, being less thorough,” the company said in an official letter to the Menteri Besar’s Office that was sighted by the national daily.
The company said it would immediately provide replacement attire that complied with the official specifications of the Jalur Gemilang.
It also said it took public criticism over the viral images seriously and would tighten its standard operating procedures, particularly for products featuring official symbols, state crests or corporate logos.
“We deeply regret any inconvenience caused and greatly appreciate the cooperation and tolerance shown by all parties involved.
“From today, the company will require customers to sign a final artwork approval form before any printing process, especially for items involving official symbols, state crests or corporate logos,” it said.
Pictures of Sanusi and several dignitaries wearing the attire drew criticism online after social media users noticed that the star on the Jalur Gemilang did not have the required 14 points.
The photographs were first published by Warta Kedah, the Kedah state government’s official media channel, before being widely shared on social media.
The clothing was worn during the Merdeka Kibar Jalur Gemilang Boat Parade yesterday, held in conjunction with Malaysia’s 69th Independence Day celebrations.
The event was jointly organised by the Anak Bukit and Suka Menanti state constituency service centres and officiated by Sanusi.
Nearly 100 boats took part in the parade from Kampung Alor Madi to the State Museum while flying the Jalur Gemilang.

Title: Parents must caution teens that mule accounts can lead to legal action, says Ewon
Article:
PENAMPANG, Aug 29 — Parents should educate and remind their children, particularly teenagers, not to become involved in mule account syndicates, which could expose them to legal action.
Sabah Deputy Chief Minister III Datuk Ewon Benedick, who is also Industrial Development, Entrepreneurship and Transport Minister, said allowing others to use their bank accounts could expose account holders to legal action if the accounts were found to have been used for fraud or other unlawful transactions.
“This is something we need to pay attention to. We need to remind ourselves, parents and children, especially teenagers, not to be easily deceived or allow their accounts to be used by others.
“Digital technology is now part of our daily lives. Therefore, while making use of technology, we also need to understand the risks and threats that come with it,” he said at the Digital Parenting Programme Series IV for the Kapayan state constituency, organised by the National Population and Family Development Board (LPPKN), here today.
Ewon, who is also Penampang Member of Parliament, said digital technology had changed how people carried out various activities, including financial transactions, business dealings and applications for government assistance.
He said QR code payments were also becoming increasingly common, including among traders at markets, showing that digital transactions were now part of everyday life.
“The same applies to the various entrepreneurship grants available nationwide. Many grant applications for entrepreneurs, associations and cooperatives, including those provided by the federal government, are now submitted online.
“However, the use of digital technology needs to be balanced so that people, especially young people, do not become too focused on their smartphones and neglect their responsibilities and other important aspects of life,” he said.
On the programme, Ewon expressed hope that the sharing sessions would enhance parents’ knowledge and help them guide their children in using digital technology safely, responsibly and wisely.
“I will continue to support parenting initiatives like this, which not only benefit the community but also remind me of my own responsibilities as a father,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Amirudin tells Umno to ‘look in the mirror’ over sincerity in election seat talks
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 29 — PKR election director Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari has pushed back against Umno’s call for sincerity in future election negotiations, saying Barisan Nasional (BN) should first examine its own approach after Pakatan Harapan (PH) previously gave up seats it had won to accommodate its unity government partner.
Utusan Malaysia
reported that Amirudin said negotiations would become difficult if one side imposed conditions before discussions had even begun.
He said PH had already demonstrated its willingness to compromise during previous state elections, including by allowing BN to contest constituencies in Selangor that had been won by PKR.
“We negotiated sincerely during the state elections, and we hope there will be the same sincerity when we hold discussions elsewhere. So remember, in Johor and Selangor, we sincerely gave way even in constituencies that we had won.
“Don’t impose conditions before discussions have even begun. If you say you will only contest seats that were lost, that makes things difficult. In Selangor, we gave BN seats that we had won.
“So when it comes to sincerity, you also have to look at yourself in the mirror. We are open to discussions, but everyone has to be sincere,” he told the national daily after officiating the Madani Kita programme with the Ampang Jaya community today.
His remarks came a day after Umno secretary-general Datuk Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said any negotiations with other parties over cooperation in the coming election must be based on sincerity and trust rather than threats or intimidation.
Amirudin, who is also Selangor menteri besar, said PH remained open to negotiating seat allocations, including constituencies beyond the 21 seats identified by Umno and BN.
“Those are indeed seats that we should consider [apart from the 21 seats]. But we will see how the discussions go. We have not even started discussions yet, so I do not want to get ahead of myself.
“But the point is that there has to be sincerity. We have negotiated sincerely before. We were even willing to share constituencies that we had won,” he said.
Amirudin also said he had been in contact with Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh, but was waiting for him to be ready to begin formal discussions.
“Rauf explained that he is waiting for several policy decisions at the Umno central and BN central levels before proceeding with discussions and so on,” he said.
Asked why PH was still prepared to work with BN despite BN having previously been described as “sakau”, a Malay term commonly used to suggest corruption or the plundering of public funds, Amirudin said such criticism had been directed at individuals rather than the party as a whole.
“It referred to individuals and not to an entire party, and we have the federal level to consider. That is why we have never said that we must work with Umno.
“We have to be prepared to cooperate with various parties. When Umno says it is willing to cooperate, okay, then we discuss it. If we were to take that view [of the entire party], we would already have changed the situation at the federal level,” he said.

Title: Desa ParkCity deaths: Post-mortems show two children were stabbed in the neck, mother suffered sharp-force wounds, says KL police chief
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 29 — Two children found dead with their parents at a Desa ParkCity home were killed by stab wounds to the neck, post-mortem examinations have confirmed.
Berita Harian
reported that Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said their mother, 47, meanwhile, died from sharp-force trauma to the neck and chest.
The findings provide the clearest account yet of how three members of the family died, as police continue investigating whether a suspected love scam and debts totalling RM260,000 were linked to the killings.
Fadil said the post-mortem on the couple’s nine-year-old daughter was carried out at the National Institute of Forensic Medicine at Kuala Lumpur Hospital yesterday.
The examination began at 9am and ended at noon.
“The post-mortem found that the cause of death was a stab wound to the neck,” he said.
The mother’s post-mortem began at about 2pm and was completed at 7.30pm.
“The post-mortem found that the cause of death was sharp-force trauma to the neck and chest,” Fadil said.
The couple’s seven-year-old son was also examined yesterday, with the post-mortem running from 2pm to 5pm.
“The post-mortem found that the victim died from a stab wound to the neck,” he said.
Fadil said the post-mortem on the children’s father, 48, described by police as the suspect, would be carried out today after examinations at the scene were completed.
“The post-mortem is expected to begin at 2pm and be completed at about 6pm today.
“All four bodies have yet to be claimed and will only be claimed after the post-mortem on the suspect has been completed,” he said.
He added that forensic personnel from HKL and the Royal Malaysia Police were at the home to carry out further examinations.
Police are also investigating claims surrounding a note allegedly linked to a love scam, including losses and debts amounting to RM260,000.
Fadil said the matter remained under investigation, but added that the family was aware of the love-scam issue and that the wife was believed to have been drawn into an illegal investment scheme.
Yesterday, investigators said they were looking into whether pressure over the RM260,000 debt, after the wife allegedly fell victim to a love scam, could have been a motive for the man to kill his wife and two children before taking his own life.
The speculation followed the discovery of a note believed to have been left by the father on the dining table of the family’s Desa ParkCity home.

Title: Putrajaya comes alive as National Day 2026 full rehearsal gets under way
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 29 — Dataran Putrajaya came alive with uniformed contingents, Jalur Gemilang and the roar of national assets during today’s full rehearsal for the 2026 National Day celebrations.
Beginning at 8 am, the rehearsal provided a preview of Monday’s celebrations, featuring corporate and government-linked companies (GLCs) and colourful special performances.
Patriotic songs and drum performances at the Gema Inovasi Madani special event helped lift the mood among thousands of people who had gathered at Dataran Putrajaya from as early as 6 am.
A Bernama check found that families from various ethnic and social backgrounds brought their children to watch the event as the school holidays began, and stayed until the rehearsal ended at 10 am.
Nurmaizatul Fatihah Hanif, 32, from Kajang, Selangor, said she and her three children had attended to show their support for her younger sibling, who is a student at Universiti Pertahanan Malaysia and is taking part in the giant flag procession.
She said it was the first time her children had seen the parade in person, having watched it only on television in previous years.
“Merdeka Day is always exciting, and watching the parade is something we look forward to. My children were especially excited when they heard the jets during the display, as we usually only see them on television. They were also thrilled to see the cute mascots,” she said.
Meanwhile, Nur Hafizza Mohd Shukri, 24, said the aerial display and K9 unit’s performance had encouraged her to return for the main celebration on Aug 31.
“I’m planning to come back here on Monday and leave home early, so I don’t miss the main events. Hopefully, it will be a lively celebration, with cooler weather and no rain,” she said.
A variety of vibrant performances and creative showcases highlighting Malaysia’s diverse arts and cultural heritage stole the spotlight during today’s full rehearsal for the 2026 National Day celebrations at Dataran Putrajaya August 29, 2026. — Bernama pic
Among the highlights of the 2026 National Day and Malaysia Day (HKHM) rehearsal was a human graphic performance involving 1,500 students from 36 schools in Selangor.
Moving in formations to the music and changing their visuals as contingents passed through the main area, the students created a dynamic display that complemented each segment of the performance.
The display of the country’s defence assets was another highlight, featuring the PT-91M Pendekar 125mm tank, Lipan Bara high-mobility armoured vehicles and Gempita multipurpose amphibious armoured vehicles in various weapon configurations, including 30mm AFV and ATGW variants.
The assets demonstrated the Malaysian Armed Forces’ capabilities and operational readiness in safeguarding national sovereignty.
A total of 10,819 participants will take part in the 2026 HKHM parade and procession, involving 76 contingents, 22 marching bands, 11 decorated vehicles, 328 land, sea, and air assets, and 112 service animals.
More than 80,000 people are expected at the 69th National Day celebrations at Dataran Putrajaya, themed “Malaysia Madani: Kesejahteraan Dinikmati”. — Bernama

Title: Durian, pineapple and RM8b in deals: Malaysia goes big at MAHA 2026
Article:
SERDANG, Aug 29 — Some 121 Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) worth about RM8 billion are expected to be signed in conjunction with the Malaysia Agriculture, Horticulture and Agrotourism Exhibition (MAHA) 2026 at the Malaysia Agro Exposition Park Serdang (Maeps) here.
Agriculture and Food Security Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu said about RM4 billion of the total would involve partnerships with China, while the remainder would involve other countries.
He said the agreements would cover technology exchange, investment opportunities, capacity building and training for farmers, including Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET), as well as creating opportunities for local agri-food products to enter export markets.
He added that the MAHA Go Global initiative would also help expand the reach of local products, particularly in Central Asia and Eastern Europe.
“That is why, through MAHA Go Global and FAMA, we hope to play a greater role in expanding markets for Malaysian products, particularly in markets where we are still lagging behind,” he told a press conference after officiating MAHA 2026 at Maeps here today.
Also present were his deputy Datuk Chan Foong Hin and the ministry’s secretary-general Datuk Seri Isham Ishak.
Mohamad identified pineapples and durians as among the local products with strong potential for expansion into international markets.
Malaysia’s pineapple exports now exceed RM1 billion, while demand for durians in China remains high, providing room for further growth, he said.
A key focus of MAHA 2026 is value creation, ensuring that local agricultural produce is not only sold as raw commodities but also processed into higher-value downstream products.
The approach is important to prevent the country from exporting raw materials and later importing processed products from overseas, he added.
“We do not want to export raw materials and then import products processed overseas. If possible, we should process them ourselves, so that value creation continues all the way to the end user in Malaysia,” he said.
The agriculture sector has also shown positive growth in its contribution to the country’s Gross Domestic Product (GDP), with the ministry expecting this to increase this year.
Efforts to boost agricultural exports need to be intensified to help balance the country’s agri-food import bill, which currently exceeds RM80 billion.
“We are now increasing our exports. That is what we are working on. Through MAHA, we can step up these efforts,” he said.
MAHA 2026 is being held from August 28 to September 6 at Maeps, featuring about 2,000 exhibitors and targeting more than four million visitors. — Bernama

Title: Jendela Phase Two to begin at 1,000 sites nationwide this year, says deputy minister
Article:
KULAI, Aug 29 — A total of 1,000 sites, including in Sabah and Sarawak, have been identified for the implementation of Phase Two of the National Digital Network (Jendela) plan this year, said Deputy Communications Minister Teo Nie Ching.
She said its implementation would ensure stronger and more stable internet coverage nationwide.
“There are 2,700 sites under the implementation of Jendela Phase Two, but for the first phase (of Phase Two) this year, 1,000 sites have been identified, and the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) has issued tenders for implementation at the sites,” she told a press conference after officiating the Japen@Petronas Jalur Gemilang Expression Programme here today.
Jendela is a government initiative coordinated by MCMC to improve digital infrastructure and internet coverage nationwide.
Meanwhile, Teo said various activities had been lined up for the public through the RIUH Merdeka programme, particularly for those planning to camp out at Dataran Putrajaya to watch the parade.
She said free public transport facilities, including shuttle buses, would also be provided at MRT Putrajaya Sentral every five minutes, while services at the Putrajaya International Convention Centre would operate every 10 minutes.
“Therefore, the public are encouraged to use public transport as many roads will be closed,” she said.
Earlier, Teo, who is also the Kulai Member of Parliament, distributed free Jalur Gemilang-shaped magnets to the public to enliven the National Month celebrations.
She said the initiative was a collaboration between the Communications Ministry, Japen and Petronas at selected petrol stations. — Bernama

Title: More than 2,300 police deployed for National Day celebrations in Putrajaya
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 29 — A total of 2,354 members and officers of the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) have been assigned to ensure the highest level of security and smooth running of the 2026 National Day celebrations at Dataran Putrajaya on Monday.
Putrajaya district police chief ACP Aidi Sham Mohamed said the assignment involved static control and traffic control at strategic locations in the area where the annual event is being held.
“For the public, I advise them to come early to Dataran Putrajaya and comply with all the regulations of the authorities.
“This includes not parking vehicles in prohibited places, not blocking traffic, and at the same time, take care of your own safety, especially the safety of children and belongings,” he said.
He told reporters after the full rehearsal of the 2026 National Day celebration attended by Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil here today.
Aidi Sham also reminded the public not to bring any dangerous weapons when attending the National Day celebration.
“Do not bring any dangerous weapons for the purpose of enlivening our National Day this year,” he said.
Earlier, Fahmi said the 2026 National Day celebration at Dataran Putrajaya on August 31, will so far be held as usual,
Themed “
Malaysia Madani: Kesejahteraan Dinikmati
”, the 69th National Day celebration will be held at Dataran Putrajaya with an expectation of more 80,000 visitors coming to witness the historic day. — Bernama

Title: Fire destroys 60pc of Pos Laju building in Bekenu, no injuries reported
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 29 — A fire destroyed about 60 per cent of a Pos Laju building in Bekenu, about 47km south-west of Miri in Sarawak, this morning, although no one was injured.
The Sarawak Fire and Rescue Department’s Operations Centre said in a statement today that it received an emergency call at 8.44am before five firefighters from the Batu Niah Fire and Rescue Station were dispatched to the scene.
The team, led by Senior Fire Officer II Azalan Azaman, arrived at about 9.30am and found the Pos Laju building, measuring about 15.2m by 12.2m, on fire.
“Initial inspections found that an estimated 60 per cent of the permanent structure had been destroyed by the fire.
“No victims were reported to have been involved or injured in the incident,” the department said.
Firefighters battled the blaze using a hose line stretching about 122m with two nozzles, while also drawing water from an open source.
The fire was brought under control at about 9.58am, while extinguishing and follow-up operations continued at the scene.
A Compact Rescue Tender and five firefighters were deployed for the operation.
The cause of the fire and the estimated losses have yet to be determined.

Title: Mask up for Merdeka: National Day crowds urged to wear N95s amid haze
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 29 — Visitors to the 2026 National Day celebrations at Dataran Putrajaya this Monday are advised to wear N95 masks to protect themselves from the effects of the current haze.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil, who is also National Day and Malaysia Day (HKHM) 2026 celebrations main committee chairman, said the advice was in line with recommendations issued by the Health Ministry (MOH), particularly for high-risk individuals.
He said the organisers of the 2026 HKHM celebrations were also providing N95 masks to more than 10,000 participants as a precautionary measure to safeguard their health.
“If they (participants) feel they need to wear a mask, they can do so. We are not making it compulsory; it is up to the individual.
“So, we advise parents bringing young children, as well as those with asthma, to bring masks, particularly N95 masks,” he told a press conference after watching the full-dress rehearsal for the celebrations here today.
Fahmi said medical teams from the Health Ministry (MOH) had also been stationed at strategic locations to provide prompt medical assistance to those who need it.
“We have locations where MOH doctors are stationed to handle emergencies. So far, I have been informed that all the medical bases are operating smoothly and no issues have been reported,” he said.
On the full-dress rehearsal, he said it went smoothly and according to the organisers’ plans.
He said a total of 823 media practitioners would be on duty during the 2026 National Day celebrations, up from about 600 last year.
“This is an encouraging and commendable increase, and I believe there will be no issues with internet access this year, making it easier for our media colleagues to cover the celebrations,” he said.
Fahmi said the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC), which manages the Network Monitoring Centre in coordination with telecommunications companies, had installed additional communications equipment at 102 National Day celebration venues to ensure smooth coverage.
On security during the celebrations, he said the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) had so far not reported any incidents requiring particular attention.
“Public order is being maintained and there are no issues at the moment,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Going to Dataran Putrajaya for National Day celebrations? Free water taxis are available from 5am on Aug 31
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 29 — Members of the public who wish to attend the 2026 National Day Celebration at Dataran Putrajaya on August 31 are urged to take advantage of the free water transport facilities provided by the Putrajaya Corporation (PPj) to facilitate movement to the celebration location.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the service not only provides convenience to the public, but also allows them to enjoy a relaxing and valuable travel experience with their families at Tasik Putrajaya.
“This year in conjunction with National Day on August 31, the Putrajaya Corporation (PPj) is providing a free water taxi service starting at 5am until 2pm on August 31,” he told Bernama after reviewing the operational preparations for the service here today.
Fahmi who is also the chairman of the 2026 National Day and Malaysia Day Celebration (HKHM) Main Committee, encouraged the public to plan their journey in advance by parking their vehicles at a location near the water transport terminal before continuing their journey using the facility to the celebration site.
“Make full use of this opportunity and I encourage you to plan your trip, you can park in places near the terminal and you can go to the site to watch the National Day parade comfortably while enjoying at Lake Putrajaya,” he said.
Based on PPj information, the free water transportation service covers the cruise taxi route between Marina Putrajaya and Anjung Floria as well as between Kelab Tasik Putrajaya and Monumen.
In addition, the water taxi service is also provided between Terra@8 and Monumen, with operations starting from 5am to 2pm on August 31.
The public is advised to refer to the travel schedule provided by PPj to check out the departure times of each route and plan their trips to the 2026 National Day Celebration in a more organised manner. — Bernama

Title: Man, 49, held in murder probe after five-year-old boy dies in Sibu
Article:
SIBU, Aug 29 — A 49-year-old man has been remanded for six days to facilitate investigations into the death of a five-year-old boy here on Friday.
Sibu police chief ACP Abang Zainal Abidin Abang Ahmad said the suspect was remanded until September 4 following a remand application at the Sibu Magistrates’ Court today.
“The case is being investigated under Section 302 of the Penal Code for murder,” he said in a statement.
Police received a report from a member of the public at about 1.45pm yesterday concerning an incident involving the boy, who was believed to have suffered an injury to his neck.
The victim was rushed to Sibu Hospital for treatment but was later pronounced dead at the hospital’s Emergency Department.
Following information received, police arrested the 49-year-old suspect believed to be involved in the incident.
Abang Zainal said several items believed to be connected to the case were also seized at the scene.
He said the suspect was currently being held at the Central Police Station lock-up.
“Section 302 of the Penal Code provides for the death penalty or imprisonment for a term of not less than 30 years and not more than 40 years.
“If the offender is not sentenced to death, the offender shall also be liable to whipping of not less than 12 strokes,” he added.
Police advised the public against speculating or disseminating unverified information, and urged them to allow investigators to conduct a thorough investigation. — The Borneo Post

Title: Anwar approves RM4.6m for upgrades at 27 Penang Islamic institutions
Article:
BUTTERWORTH, Aug 29 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has approved an additional RM4.6 million this year to upgrade basic infrastructure at 27 Islamic educational institutions across Penang.
The allocation is an increase from the RM2.11 million provided last year for upgrading works at 11 Islamic educational institutions in the state.
Anwar, who is also finance minister, said the allocation would be used for various upgrading works at the institutions.
“Last year in Penang, we added more than RM2 million. This year, I announced RM4.6 million for people’s religious institutions.
“It is for upgrading works, including walls and fences, madrasahs, schools, new kindergarten buildings and tahfiz academies,” he said when speaking at the National Tadabbur Perdana and Maidah Wanita Madani Permatang Pauh programmes at Masjid Muhajirin here today.
He said the government would continue to focus on the needs of people’s religious schools and Islamic educational institutions to strengthen religious education facilities in the country.
Anwar also said efforts to strengthen Islamic education should keep pace with technological developments, including the use of artificial intelligence (AI) in Quranic and Islamic studies.
However, he stressed that technology must be guided by good values and strong moral principles.
“AI must have values. AI must be rooted in morality. It should not be used simply to develop talent and understanding without values and morality,” he said.
The prime minister also urged the public to make use of the freedom available in the country to organise more religious programmes to strengthen their understanding of Islam.
He said programmes such as Quran classes, tadabbur sessions and religious talks should be held continuously to deepen public understanding and appreciation of the true teachings of Islam. — Bernama

Title: Smoke from West Kalimantan pushes four Sarawak locations into ‘very unhealthy’ zone
Article:
KUCHING, Aug 29 — Four locations in Sarawak recorded very unhealthy air quality as of noon on Saturday, after Serian joined Lubok Antu, Lundu and Sri Aman in registering Air Pollutant Index (API) readings above 200.
According to the Natural Resources and Environment Board’s (NREB) Daily Haze Watch, Lubok Antu recorded the highest API reading at 230, followed by Lundu (228), Sri Aman (227) and IPD Serian (204).
Eight other locations remained at the unhealthy level — Sarikei (193), Tebedu (182), Kuching (174), Samarahan (173), Mukah (168), Sibu (163), Kapit (155) and Bintulu (153).
The remaining six locations recorded moderate air quality — Samalaju (96), Miri (68), ILP Miri (67), Bario (66), Lawas (59) and Limbang (52).
An API reading of between 51 and 100 is classified as moderate, 101 to 200 as unhealthy, and 201 to 300 as very unhealthy.
Meanwhile, Department of Environment (DoE) deputy director-general (Development) Azuri Azizah Saedon said moderate to dense transboundary smoke from West Kalimantan had been detected moving northwards into western Sarawak.
Citing an Asean Specialised Meteorological Centre (ASMC) report dated Aug 28, she said NOAA-20 satellite imagery detected 1,738 hotspots in Kalimantan, 36 in Sumatra and six in Malaysia — five in Sarawak and one in Sabah.
She said dry conditions persisted across much of the southern Asean region, with scattered to widespread hotspot clusters detected in Kalimantan as well as central and southern Sumatra.
“Several air quality monitoring stations in West Kalimantan, western Sarawak and Peninsular Malaysia, as well as central and southern Sumatra, also recorded unhealthy to very unhealthy readings,” she said in a statement on Saturday.
Azuri said DoE had stepped up enforcement and daily patrols in areas prone to open burning, while the National Open Burning Action Plan and National Haze Action Plan had been activated.
Under the National Haze Action Plan, the National Disaster Management Agency (NADMA) will activate disaster management committees at the district, state or federal level when API readings exceed 150 for more than 24 hours.
Outdoor classroom activities are to be stopped when the API exceeds 100, while schools, kindergartens and childcare centres are to close immediately when readings exceed 200.
“If the trend in readings shows an increase towards 200, preparations must be made to close the affected schools, kindergartens and childcare centres,” she said.
Cloud-seeding operations may also be carried out when API readings remain above 150 for more than 24 hours, subject to suitable cloud and weather conditions.
Azuri also reminded the public against open burning, adding that offences under the Environmental Quality (Amendment) Act 2024 carry a fine of between RM25,000 and RM1 million, imprisonment of up to five years, or both.
The public is also urged to cooperate by extinguishing small fires and reporting cases of open burning or fires to the Fire and Rescue Department via 999 or the DoE through its toll-free line at 1-800-88-2727. — The Borneo Post

Title: ‘How could I forget?’ Anwar calls Permatang Pauh his hometown and birthplace of political journey
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 29 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has said he has never forgotten Permatang Pauh, describing his former constituency as his “hometown” and the place where his political journey began.
Although he now represents Tambun, Anwar said Permatang Pauh continued to hold deep sentimental value for him,
Sinar Harian
reported.
“It is true that now that I am prime minister, I am the elected representative for Tambun. But where did it all begin? Permatang Pauh... how could I forget? This is our hometown,” he was quoted as saying.
Anwar was speaking at the Permatang Pauh Skim Usahawan Bangkit (SUB) programme at Dewan Yayasan Aman Penanti in Kubang Semang, Bukit Mertajam, today.
Anwar previously served as Permatang Pauh MP before later contesting in Port Dickson and Tambun.
He said his attachment to Permatang Pauh was also why he had asked organisers to bring the SUB programme to the constituency.
“Remembering that Permatang Pauh is my place, I asked the organisers to hold the SUB programme here.
“It is fine if you hold it in Bukit Gantang or Trong, but you have to come down to Permatang Pauh because this is my place, my hometown. And this is the proof — today, SUB is being held in the Permatang Pauh parliamentary constituency,” he said.

Title: National Day celebrations at Dataran Putrajaya to proceed as planned, says Fahmi
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 29 — The 2026 National Day celebrations at Dataran Putrajaya on August 31 will proceed as planned for now, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said.
The chairman of the 2026 National Day and Malaysia Day (HKHM) Celebrations main committee said the decision was made at a special meeting with several agencies yesterday in view of the current haze situation at the venue.
“We have decided that if the haze situation remains as it is this morning, as was the case yesterday, we will proceed with the event on Monday (August 31),” he told a press conference after watching the full dress rehearsal for the celebrations here today.
Fahmi said the authorities would continue to assess the haze situation, including the possibility of cloud seeding.
“(Cloud seeding) will depend on whether there are clouds suitable for seeding. So, Nadma’s (National Disaster Management Agency) assessment will be conveyed to the committee.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil inspects the full rehearsal for the 2026 National Day parade at Dataran Putrajaya August 29, 2026. — Bernama pic
“We hope cloud seeding can be carried out today or tomorrow, but everything is subject to the views and findings of the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia),” he said.
He said more than 80,000 visitors were expected this year, with the school holidays and the transport facilities provided by the organisers expected to contribute to the turnout.
“This year, Prasarana Malaysia Bhd is providing 24-hour MRT services, so it will make it easier for those who want to attend.
“We also have other modes of transport, including buses from MRT stations to the venue, as well as water taxis. With all these facilities in place, we expect a large turnout,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Anwar vows to claw back billions lost to leakages and return money to Malaysians
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 29 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said billions of ringgit lost through leakages and misuse must be recovered and returned to Malaysians, arguing that the government could not justify allowing vast sums of public money to disappear while ordinary people received relatively modest amounts in assistance.
Sinar Harian
reported that Anwar said the government had a duty to act against the loss or misuse of public funds, although any action must be based on investigations and evidence.
“I want to stop that, take the money back and give it back to the people. That’s all. And for that, I get cursed in all sorts of ways.
“If people only want RM2,000, but what you took and allowed to disappear runs into billions of ringgit, I want to stop that, take it back and give it back to the people,” he was quoted as saying.
Anwar was speaking today at the
Skim Usahawan Bangkit (SUB) Madani Permatang Pauh
programme at Dewan Yayasan Aman Penanti in Kubang Semang, Bukit Mertajam.
He said firm action against leakages could invite criticism, but that the government had to uphold good governance and ensure public money ultimately benefited the people.
Anwar cited allegations involving Lembaga Tabung Haji and RM12 billion in funds as an example of a matter that should be investigated to establish what happened and who, if anyone, was responsible.
“I said RM12 billion went missing. How did it disappear? When did it disappear? Who allowed it to disappear? Investigate.
“If there is an investigation and there is evidence, haul them in. If there is strong evidence, charge them in court. Then leave it to the judge,” he said.
Anwar stressed that guilt or innocence should be determined by the courts rather than by the executive.
“If he is not guilty, let him go. If he is guilty, go to Sungai Buloh, go to Kajang, wherever it may be. That is how we govern,” he said.
He said the government was also seeking to ensure that allocations and assistance reached their intended recipients instead of being siphoned off.
“In the past, sometimes those at the top took a lot. If it was rightfully theirs, that would be fine. How much are we giving now? RM800, up to a maximum of RM4,000. But what went missing was tens of billions,” he said.
Anwar added that criticism would not deter him from pursuing the issue.
“I say, curse me as much as you want. I don’t even take a salary.
“I want to show that not every elected representative, not every minister, not every leader goes to work just to take other people’s money. That is the message I want to send,” he said.

Title: Anwar: Tabung Haji RCI probe crucial to prevent further losses and identify those responsible for the RM12b shortfall
Article:
BUKIT MERTAJAM, Aug 29 — The investigation into issues raised in the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) Report on Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) will continue to ensure that the country does not suffer furrther losses, said Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
The prime minister stressed that appropriate action must be taken if the investigation finds that wrongdoing had occurred, but the process must be based on evidence and the law.
“As in the Tabung Haji (RCI investigation), if no action is taken, the country will suffer losses, but when action is taken, I get criticised. I don’t understand.
“I said RM12 billion was lost. How was it lost? When was it lost? Investigate who was responsible for the loss. If there is evidence, charge them in court and then leave it to the judge. That is how we govern and administer the country,” he said when launching the Madani Permatang Pauh Usahawan Bangkit Scheme (SUB) at Dewan Yayasan Aman, Penanti, here today.
Anwar said the government would not punish anyone without due process, but would not compromise if there was strong evidence of wrongdoing.
On July 29, the Department of Islamic Development Malaysia (Jakim) published the 211-page RCI Report on the investigation into the management and operations of TH for the period from 2014 to 2020.
The report contains various findings relating to weaknesses in the management of the institution during the period, as well as 25 recommendations for improvement, 75 per cent of which had been implemented by TH as of July 30.
Elaborating, Anwar said efforts to curb leakages must continue as Malaysia has substantial financial resources, but some of the benefits do not reach the people due to leakages in the management of government funds and allocations.
He said efforts to curb leakages were part of the government’s responsibility to ensure that every allocation provided could benefit the people, particularly those in need.
“What is the purpose of taking action? To prevent leakages. Who says Malaysia is poor? It is not (that the assistance is lacking), but it does not reach the grassroots because a lot of it leaks along the way,” he said.
The prime minister stressed that the government remained committed to helping all segments of society through the implementation of various programmes and initiatives that directly address the needs of the people.
He said government assistance should include efforts to help the people generate income, obtain education, and acquire skills and technological knowledge.
He said the government had provided various forms of assistance, including through Amanah Ikhtiar Malaysia, Tabung Ekonomi Kumpulan Usaha Niaga Nasional (Tekun Nasional), Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) and Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA), but efforts to empower the people to become self-reliant must continue to be strengthened.
Anwar also said the government would continue to strengthen the role of the National Information Dissemination Centre (NADI), particularly in bringing access to technology and artificial intelligence (AI) to rural areas.
“Malaysia is the only country where we bring AI and technology to the districts. Every state constituency has one NADI.
“We have achieved global recognition because we have established NADI even in Pulau Banggi, at the tip of Sabah. However, this is still not enough because many people do not know what NADI is. Many children are not making use of it,” he said.
Earlier, Anwar presented certificates to six successful applicants under the Skim Usahawan Bangkit programme in Permatang Pauh. — Bernama

Title: Anwar to unveil initiatives addressing people’s daily concerns in National Day speech
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 29 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim will announce several key initiatives in his National Day address at the Putrajaya International Convention Centre (PICC) tomorrow afternoon.
In a Facebook post, Anwar said he would touch on issues affecting the people, their daily lives and the responsibility of the current generation to appreciate the country’s independence.
“Insya-Allah, I will deliver the National Day address tomorrow afternoon.
“Nearly seven decades have passed since the country gained independence. We remember the struggles and sacrifices of previous generations who paved the way with their sweat, blood and tears.
“At the same time, we must reflect on the responsibility of the current generation to uphold and give meaning to our independence,” he said.
In the same post, Anwar urged Malaysians to celebrate National Day by strengthening the spirit of unity and rejecting any incitement that could fuel hatred among people of different races and religions.
He said this was important to ensure that peace and the well-being of the people are preserved. — Bernama

Title: DOE: Sri Aman’s API hits 221 as 28 areas nationwide record unhealthy air quality
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 29 — Air quality in Sri Aman, Sarawak, remained at a very unhealthy level this morning, with the Air Pollutant Index (API) reaching 221 as of 9 am, while 28 other areas nationwide recorded unhealthy readings.
Department of Environment (DOE) Deputy Director-General (Development) Azuri Azizah Saedon said in a statement today that another 39 areas recorded moderate air quality.
In Sarawak, areas recording unhealthy API readings included Serian (194), Sarikei (190), Kuching (169), Samarahan (168), Mukah (165), Sibu (161), Kapit (154) and Bintulu (150).
In Peninsular Malaysia, unhealthy air quality was recorded in Sungai Petani (161), Langkawi (157) and Alor Setar (155) in Kedah; Minden (160), Seberang Perai (157) and Seberang Jaya (156) in Penang; Cheras (160) and Batu Muda (155) in Kuala Lumpur; and Putrajaya (155).
Other affected areas were Taiping (155), Tanjung Malim (154), Tasek Ipoh (151) and Seri Manjung (110) in Perak; Shah Alam (154), Johan Setia (153) and Petaling Jaya (133) in Selangor; Nilai (152) and Seremban (136) in Negeri Sembilan; Kangar, Perlis (155); and Segamat, Johor (142).
Azuri Azizah said the country’s air quality deteriorated today due to the movement of haze smoke from various directions.
She said that, based on a report issued yesterday by the Singapore-based Asean Specialised Meteorological Centre (ASMC) and satellite imagery from NOAA-20, 1,738 hotspots were detected in Kalimantan and 36 in Sumatra, while six hotspots were detected within Malaysia — one in Sabah and five in Sarawak.
“The Regional Haze Map issued by the ASMC on Aug 28 indicates persistent dry weather conditions across most parts of the southern Asean region, except for parts of Peninsular Malaysia and northern Borneo, which received rainfall.
“Widespread clusters of hotspots were detected in Kalimantan and in the southern and central parts of Sumatra, while scattered hotspots were detected in other parts of the southern Asean region,” she said.
She added that moderate to dense transboundary smoke plumes were detected over West Kalimantan, moving northwards into western Sarawak, while moderate to dense smoke plumes were observed in other parts of Kalimantan, as well as central and southern Sumatra.
“Meanwhile, light to moderate localised smoke plumes were detected in eastern Java.
“Several air quality monitoring stations in West Kalimantan, western Sarawak, Peninsular Malaysia, and southern and central Sumatra recorded readings ranging from unhealthy to very unhealthy,” she said. — Bernama
